info.bio:
Minor Threat fue una banda estadounidense de hardcore punk. La banda estuvo activa desde 1980 hasta 1983, siempre dentro de la, entonces, activa escena hardcore de Washington DC, EE.UU., denominada posteriormente DC Hardcore.

Su estilo se caracterizó por canciones con mensajes directos en sus letras que eran ejecutadas muy rápidamente, algunas veces en menos de un minuto. Poco a poco fueron alargando el tempo y dotando a éstas de una mayor complejidad compositiva.

scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El punk como «violento, rápido y ruidoso» tarda en conquistar EE UU, pero cuando lo hace el hardcore se convierte durante dos décadas en el idioma nacional de millones de chavales. Misfits y el «scum-rock»; el crossover punk-metal (Suicidal Tendencies, Corrosion Of Conformity, Agnostic Front); Mission Of Burma en Boston. Washington: Bad Brains (reggae, funk y metal diez años por delante), Minor Threat (el «straight-edge») y Rites Of Spring, inventores del emo-core. San Francisco: Dead Kennedys de Jello Biafra, D.R.I. (thrash antes que Metallica), Flipper. Los «beach punks» de Los Ángeles: Germs, X, Black Flag (Damaged), Descendents, Gun Club (Fire Of Love), Bad Religion. El jazz-core de Minutemen y Saccharine Trust; en el Medio Oeste, Husker Du y Replacements cambian el hardcore para siempre; en Chicago, Naked Raygun y Big Black de Steve Albini; en Europa, The Ex y los italianos CCCP.

podcast.title: DIY Ethic and Label Principles
podcast.body: Minor Threat's leader, Ian MacKaye, became a punk rock legend due to the band's music and the strong ethics they established. They adopted a serious do-it-yourself (DIY) ethic, founding Dischord Records, which would release material for other hardcore bands. Dischord had strict policies of keeping record prices low and affordable. "Leader Ian McKay became a punk rock legend, two reasons. First of all, Minor Threats music found a lot of fans, but just as important was the ethics that he and the band laid down. They had a serious do-it-yourself ethic, founding a record label called Discord that would eventually release material by other hardcore bands. Second, they had a strict policy of keeping record prices low and affordable."

podcast.title: Formation and Inspiration
podcast.body: Minor Threat formed in 1980, primarily because its members were huge fans of Bad Brains. They reformed under the name Minor Threat after initially being known as Teen Idols. "They came together because the members loved Bad Brains. After starting out as a group known as Teen Idols, they reformed as Minor Threat in 1980."

xref.title: Cousin Tracy Bradford's Punk Introduction
xref.body: His non-blood relative "cousin," Tracy Bradford, who was two years his senior and lived in Evanston, Illinois, introduced him to authentic punk rock culture. She appeared in bondage pants and motorcycle boots with an anti-P.C. t-shirt, showcasing a record collection including first singles from Misfits and Minor Threat, and connected him to the underground network of fanzines and show flyers from across the country. "She had an antiposti t-shirt and two's punk. I was just like, oh my God, I was so into it."

xref.title: Musical Beginnings
xref.body: Dela Roka started playing guitar at the age of eight. By his teenage years, he was deeply engrossed in punk music, citing bands like The Clash, Minor Threat, Bad Brains, and Bad Religion as significant influences. "He picked up a guitar at eight, and by the time he was a teenager, Zach was deep into punk, clash, minor threat, bad brains, bad religion, that kind of thing."
